purpose: Model comparison across intelligence and price classes, to test whether Git Why's value is making weak models smarter or making strong models cheaper.

hypothesis.statement: Git Why's measurable benefit is turn and token reduction for CAPABLE models, not accuracy gain for weak ones.
hypothesis.priorEvidence: With deepseek-v4-flash (capable) it halved median tool calls, 16 to 9, at identical accuracy on 7 of 8 paired tasks. With gemini-2.5-flash-lite (weak) accuracy separated but zg explained more of the gain than git why did, whose paired edge was one task wide at n=7.
hypothesis.predicts: Tool-call and token reduction should GROW with model capability, and accuracy gain should shrink. If the opposite holds -- weak models gaining accuracy while strong models save nothing -- the hypothesis is wrong and the cost story inverts.
hypothesis.whyItMatters: A turn saved on an expensive model is worth real money; a turn saved on a cheap one is close to free. Which end the benefit lands on decides how the tool should be positioned.

ordering: Tiers run in order. A tier only runs if the one before it produced valid trials with reconciled token accounting -- the harness has produced eight plausible-but-wrong results in this project's history, and none of them announced itself. Cheap models are how that gets caught before it is expensive.

tiers.name: validation
tiers.purpose: Prove the harness is sound. Not a comparison.
tiers.gate: Trials valid, tokens non-null and reconciled against the provider's own accounting, tool calls counted, arm A has no treatment.

tiers.name: cheap tier comparison
tiers.gate: A visible difference between arms on at least one measure. If every arm ties at every tier the benchmark cannot discriminate and going further wastes money.
tiers.note: gemini-2.5-flash-lite was run before this design was written down and is listed here because it belongs to this price class, not because it was planned as part of the tier.

tiers.name: frontier
tiers.note: openai/ is the direct-credit provider, not DevPass.

tiers.name: most expensive, last
tiers.note: Run only after every other tier has produced usable numbers. Explicitly last at the owner's instruction because it burns usage fastest.

arms.A: baseline: git, ripgrep, no retrieval tooling

measures: citation accuracy against the hand-verified commit
tool calls to reach the answer, paired per task
input and output tokens, summed across every step_finish event
observed cost, from provider accounting rather than estimated from a price list
cost per correct answer, which is the number that actually decides whether this is worth installing
reportingRules: Every rate carries its numerator and denominator.
Exit categories stay separate: completed, timed out, budget exceeded, never started. A trial that did not run is not a wrong answer.
Paired comparisons only, on tasks both arms attempted. Arm medians alone let task difficulty drive the result.
Descriptive only. No significance claims at these sample sizes.
